name: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like papillary dermal elastolysis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: PXE-like papillary dermal elastolysis diagnostic criteria

criteria.description: Presence of asymptomatic, yellowish papules arranged in a reticular pattern predominantly on the neck and supraclavicular areas
Histological evidence of loss or fragmentation of elastic fibers in the papillary dermis without calcification
Absence of systemic involvement and negative genetic testing for ABCC6 mutations to exclude true pseudoxanthoma elasticum
Dermoscopy showing whitish linear streaks and yellowish clods correlating with elastolysis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical presentation, histopathology, and exclusion of true PXE) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and histopathological; genetic testing helps exclude PXE.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Yellowish papular lesions in a reticular pattern
pathognomonic.notes: Typically located on the lateral neck and supraclavicular regions
searchTerms: yellowish small raised skin spots in net-like pattern
yellow papules arranged in mesh pattern

pathognomonic.symptomName: Loss of elastic fibers in papillary dermis on biopsy
pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by histopathology with special elastic stains
searchTerms: loss of elastic fibers in upper skin layer
damaged elastic tissue in papillary dermis
elastic fiber reduction on skin biopsy

common.notes: Patients usually do not report pruritus or pain

common.symptomName: Wrinkling and laxity of affected skin
common.notes: Mild skin laxity may be present in affected areas

searchTerms: white linear streaks seen on skin exam
linear white marks on skin surface

occasional.symptomName: Mild skin atrophy in affected regions
occasional.notes: Localized thinning of the skin may be observed
searchTerms: mild thinning of skin in affected areas
skin thinning localized to certain regions

occasional.notes: Dilated superficial blood vessels occasionally seen
searchTerms: small visible blood vessels over skin bumps
red spider veins on skin lesions
slight darkening of skin around lesions

rare.symptomName: Calcification of elastic fibers on histology
rare.notes: Rarely observed, helps differentiate from PXE
searchTerms: calcium deposits in elastic skin fibers

imaging: Dermoscopy showing whitish linear streaks and yellowish clods
genetic: No pathogenic mutations in ABCC6 gene (excludes PXE)
other: Histopathology: loss or fragmentation of elastic fibers in papillary dermis without calcification

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic involvement including cardiovascular and ophthalmological manifestations
Calcification of elastic fibers on histology
Elastic fiber loss primarily in mid-dermis rather than papillary dermis
Clinical presentation with fine wrinkling rather than papular lesions

redFlags: Presence of systemic symptoms such as angioid streaks or cardiovascular abnormalities
Histological evidence of calcified elastic fibers
Positive ABCC6 mutation indicating true pseudoxanthoma elasticum
references: Neldner KH. Pseudoxanthoma elasticum. Clin Dermatol. 1988;6(1):1-159.
Baccarani-Contri M, et al. Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like papillary dermal elastolysis: a clinicopathologic study. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2001;44(6):1021-1026.
